comment: Degree and stated finance tenure are plausible from the excerpt; years are inferred rather than tied to dated accounting roles. Follow-up is specific (accreditation).

Degree and office-suite quote support some claims, but finance tenure is treated as payroll tenure; the laws/regulations quote only shows payroll projections. The follow-up names the partial must-have.
Accounting bachelor supports the education claim; no payroll evidence is shown, and ADP/Dynamics are reasonable listed gaps. The follow-up is specific.
Degree and Excel keywords are supported, but generic finance years do not establish manufacturing costing; GAAP/SOX knowledge is not evidenced. SAP is a useful next check.
Direct quotes support procedures, reconciliation, Office, and Solomon/GL claims; GAAP is not evidenced. The single missing requirement is clear to verify.

The budget quote supports expense budgeting; degree/years claims are plausible. The reporting quote is broad compliance reporting, not month-end close/commentary; the follow-up lacks a concrete verification prompt.
Business-management education may be related, but 0 finance-relevant years leaves 5+ similar-role experience unsupported without role-specific evidence. Software/construction gaps appear complete.
Accounting degree and direct GAAP/Excel snippets support the statuses; years imply manufacturing-costing experience without showing that domain. SAP is a useful next check.
The accounting associate claim is explicit; payroll and listed systems are not evidenced. The follow-up is direct.
The SOX/financial-audit quote shows some exposure, but 0 finance years is used to assess 4+ audit years despite the audit language. Several specific requirements remain uncertain.

The close-process quote supports month-end reporting and the budget-tool quote supports budgeting, but the explanation gives 9 years and also says dates cannot be computed. That internal inconsistency reduces trust.
The Excel listing supports partial proficiency; no evidence supports manufacturing costing or an accounting/finance bachelor’s. The gap list tracks the must-have criteria shown.
Training and business-development snippets are plausible, but Master of Tax/JD/LLM is marked partial yet omitted from Gaps. Tenure is inferred from the finance-years measure.
The education mismatch is surfaced, but manufacturing costing is marked partial despite 0 finance-relevant years and no domain evidence. The list otherwise covers the must-haves.
A civil-engineering master’s is claimed to meet both the accounting/related bachelor’s and tax/JD requirement; neither is supported. Both credential gaps are omitted from Gaps.

The Excel financial-system quote supports Excel; Business Studies and general finance tenure do not by themselves prove an accounting degree or manufacturing costing. Major software/accounting gaps are listed.
A Master of Commerce and explicit payroll-administration quote support both must-haves; ADP and Dynamics are clear optional gaps.
Audit-process and workpaper quotes support some audit exposure, but 21.3 finance years do not establish 4+ audit years. Big 4/public-company, supervisory, and PCAOB criteria remain unverified.
SAP implementation is not direct evidence of Timberline/Sage 300; the related degree and finance years are plausible. Construction/WIP gaps are listed and the next check is concrete.
Direct GAAP, reconciliation, and systems quotes support the claims; Office-suite absence cannot be verified from the excerpt. The Microsoft Office follow-up is specific.
The Accountancy degree is supported; 13.3 finance years do not prove construction-specific similar work. Software, construction, and WIP gaps align with the stated criteria.

The finance/operations master’s supports related education; Oracle and Hyperion show accounting systems but not advanced Excel specifically, appropriately marked partial. The years follow-up is relevant.
The generic “banking and financial services background” supports the domain claim only weakly; 2.2 years versus 5–7 is plausible partial. Listed mandatory gaps appear complete.
Accounting degree, finance tenure, and Sage/ACCPAC terms give some support; none directly names Sage 300, so partial is cautious. The follow-up is focused.

The related finance master’s and tenure estimate are plausible, but a generic software/computer-programs phrase weakly supports Timberline. Criteria gaps seem complete; the follow-up names the main blocker.
Finance years and the SOX-compliance phrase do not substantiate audit tenure, Big 4 work, or supervisory audit experience. Gaps are listed, but asking only about CPA may miss other major checks.

The degree and budget values are grounded in snippets, but finance tenure does not prove leadership; reporting/budget quotes only partially support the nice-to-haves. The verification target is broad.
Accounting-close, GAAP, reconciliation, and Office keywords support the statuses; the Office-suite claim is reasonably partial. The missing item is clearly identified.
High-school education plainly does not meet an associate-degree requirement; labeling this gap partial rather than not met understates it. Payroll/software gaps are clear.
The 5.2 finance years do not prove 4+ years of audit work; snippets show some SOX audit exposure but not tenure or Big 4/supervisory/PCAOB depth. CPA is only one of several checks.
